discretion

/dih-SKRESH-uhn/ - the stress falls on SKRESH · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Discretion means good judgment about what to reveal and what to keep private.

The night manager checked famous guests in with quiet discretion, logging suites under borrowed names.

Worked Example

When the quiz-team captain opened his inbox and found next week's answer sheet, forwarded from an address he recognized, he thought for a long minute. Then he deleted the file, told the coach only that the questions should be reprinted "to be safe," and never spoke the sender's name. The team kept its title and its honor, and one classmate quietly got the second chance he needed.

That long minute is discretion at work: good judgment about what to say and what to keep private. The captain neither lied nor tattled; he weighed what each listener needed to know and released exactly that much. Discretion is not secrecy — secrecy hides everything — and not shyness either. It is judgment, applied to the mouth.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

reticence: Reticence is the standing habit of saying little, whatever the subject — a temperament that defaults to silence. Discretion is a judgment made case by case: it can talk freely all afternoon and still keep the one fact that matters private. The reticent stay quiet; the discreet choose.

diplomacy: Diplomacy is the art of managing people and their competing interests — smoothing tempers, finding words both sides can accept. Discretion manages the information itself: deciding what may be revealed and what stays private. A diplomat needs discretion constantly, but diplomacy aims at the relationship, discretion at the disclosure.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

indiscretion: the blurted remark or leaked detail itself

carelessness: letting things slip with no judgment applied anywhere

Where it sits · how much information gets held back — tact → discretion → secrecy

tact vs. discretion: Tact softens how news is delivered; discretion goes further and weighs whether some of it should travel at all.

secrecy vs. discretion: Secrecy goes past discretion — nothing is released to anyone, even when a fair question deserves an answer.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-

Prefix — dis-: apart

Root — cret

Root — cret: sifted, separated (Latin cernere, cretus)

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: act or quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Dis- (apart) + cret- (sifted, from cernere) + -ion (quality of) = the quality of sifting apart. Discretion is a sorting gift: this fact may travel, that one stays home. Latin used discretio for exactly that power of separating — and the person who has it still sorts every sentence before it leaves.

Use the root in a new word: discreet

Use the root in a new word: discreet: Make a discreet inquiry about the ring size — nothing that gives the surprise away.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / professional

Discretion is the working word for judgment about disclosure — what to say, to whom, and when to say nothing. It is not this unit's discernible, despite the shared Latin root: discernible describes what can be noticed; discretion decides what should be told. Reach for tact when the question is phrasing, secrecy when nothing may come out at all, and discretion for the judgment that sorts between them.
